title: Derived direct-image comparisons commute with open restriction and reassociation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings $\Lambda_T$ and the finite-subextension convention of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed; sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded categories $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$ and their total right derived module direct images [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories; sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Write $\kappa_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*$ for the resolution-normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Then:

1. For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow hT$, the two maps from $R(hgf)_*$ to $Rh_*Rg_*Rf_*$ agree:
$$ (Rh_*\kappa_{g,f})\circ\kappa_{h,gf}=(\kappa_{h,g}Rf_*)\circ\kappa_{hg,f}. $$
2. For $f:S\to T$ and a quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, put $S_U=S\times_TU$, with open $j_S:S_U\hookrightarrow S$ and restricted map $f_U:S_U\to U$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\rho_{f,j}:j^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R(f_U)_*j_S^*.$$
For a K-injective representative $I$ of an object of $D_S$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], this is the class of the canonical underived restriction isomorphism $j^*f_*I\cong(f_U)_*j_S^*I$, whose value on a site object $V\to U$ is the identity on $I(V\times_T S)$. Module structures are transported along the inverse coefficient-ring comparisons of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients].
3. These restriction isomorphisms commute with successive open restrictions. They also commute with composition: for $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gT$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, let $j_Y:Y_U\hookrightarrow Y$, $j_X:X_U\hookrightarrow X$ be the pulled-back opens. The two maps from $j^*R(gf)_*$ to $R(g_U)_*R(f_U)_*j_X^*$ agree:
$$ (R(g_U)_*\rho_{f,j_Y})\circ(\rho_{g,j}Rf_*)\circ(j^*\kappa_{g,f})=(\kappa_{g_U,f_U}j_X^*)\circ\rho_{gf,j}. $$
All formulas insert the canonical functor associators and fibre-product identifications; for identity maps and identity open immersions the comparisons are identities.

source.place: The composition isomorphism, equality Rq_*Rr_* = R(qr)_*; Canonicity and associativity, restriction normalization of all comparison maps. Extracted from returned Step 2.

proof.text: Throughout, identify $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$ with the category of sheaves of modules over the section-ring sheaf of $\Lambda_T$ by the equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]; it leaves underlying abelian sheaves, section groups, restriction maps and morphisms unchanged, so the module direct images, inverse images and comparisons below are the ringed-site ones, and the ringed-site statements cited below apply to $D_T$. For every morphism $a$, the module adjunction $a^*\dashv a_*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] has exact left adjoint by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $u=a_*$ and $v=a^*$: $a_*I$ is K-injective whenever $I$ is. For an open $j$, [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] gives the exact additive left adjoint $j_!\dashv j^*$, so the same lemma also makes $j^*I$ K-injective. These applications are in module categories over the pulled-back ring sheaves, not in constant discrete-coefficient categories. The small-site module categories have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Thus all the iterated direct images and open restrictions used below can be computed on the same initial K-injective complex.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; module adjunctions and exactness as cited

proof.text: Fix a K-injective representative $I$. In the normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], take the resolution $f_*I\to J$ to be the identity of $f_*I$, which is allowed by step 1. Consequently $\kappa_{g,f,QI}$ is the class of the inverse of the underived comparison $g_*f_*I\cong(gf)_*I$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. This identifies the specified comparison, rather than choosing a new isomorphism. The arbitrary-resolution formulas in [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] show how to use these representatives functorially: a derived arrow $QI\to QI'$ is represented by a unique homotopy class $t:I\to I'$, its direct-image arrow is the class of $a_*t$, and a change of representative is the corresponding image of a homotopy equivalence. Hence the computations below determine natural transformations and remain valid under the canonical resolution identifications.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070Y, lemma-K-injective and lemma-K-injective-defined; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6E normalization

proof.text: For clause 1 compute on $I$ as in step 2. The underlying composition comparison is restriction along the fibre-product isomorphism of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]. On a site object $V\to T$, both bracketings identify the iterated fibre product with $V\times_T X$. Both isomorphisms have the same projections to $V$ and $X$: all intermediate projections are forgotten by composition. The universal property of the fibre product therefore makes the two isomorphisms equal. Applying the contravariant sections functor $I^n$ gives equal maps in every degree $n$, compatible with the differential. The module comparisons are precisely the lifts of these sheaf comparisons by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]; their linearity uses the coefficient-composition equation of [lem-sfb-eta-comp]. Equality of their underlying sheaf maps is equality of module maps, since a module morphism is a sheaf map satisfying a property. Taking their classes and the identifications of step 2 gives exactly the displayed associativity equation.

source.place: Canonicity and associativity: composition of proper direct images is associative; explicit sectionwise argument

proof.text: Through the equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] (step 1), apply [lem-sfb-proetale-open-restriction-counit] with $R=\Lambda_T$ and $X=S$, $Y=T$, $W=U$. Its coefficient rings are actual inverse-image rings. Transport them to $\Lambda_S,\Lambda_U,\Lambda_{S_U}$ using the canonical ring isomorphisms of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]; its final assertion identifies each module inverse image with the lift of the sheaf inverse image using $\alpha^{-1}$. This gives a natural module isomorphism $\beta_{f,j}:j^*f_*\cong(f_U)_*j_S^*$. The cited open comparison states its evaluation: on $V\to U$ it is the identification $M(S\times_TV)\cong M(S_U\times_UV)$. Under the canonical fibre-product identification this is the identity on the section module. Thus the comparison has exactly the coefficient action and the underived normalization required in clause 2, without assuming that $\Lambda$ is finite or discrete.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; open-slice comparison and general ring-sheaf version as stated by the cited node

proof.text: For $K\cong QI$, step 1 makes $j_S^*I$ K-injective, so $j^*Rf_*K$ is represented by $j^*f_*I$ and $R(f_U)_*j_S^*K$ by $(f_U)_*j_S^*I$. Define $\rho_{f,j,K}$ to be the class of $\beta_{f,j,I}$ from step 4. Both $\beta$ and its inverse are chain maps, since the underived isomorphism is natural and thus commutes with every differential. They give an isomorphism in the derived category. For a chain map $t:I\to I'$, naturality of $\beta$ gives $\beta_{I'}(j^*f_*t)=((f_U)_*j_S^*t)\beta_I$. The representative and transition formulas of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] identify these terms with the corresponding derived arrows; the same equality for the homotopy equivalence changing $I$ proves independence of the representative. This proves existence, naturality, and the K-injective formula of clause 2.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070Y; descend the natural open comparison on K-injectives

proof.text: For successive opens $W\xrightarrow{v}U\xrightarrow{j}T$, evaluate both the direct restriction comparison and the composite of the two comparisons on a K-injective $I$, in degree $n$, at $V\to W$. By step 4 both identify the section module with $I^n(V\times_T S)$ and act as the identity after the canonical fibre-product identifications. The ring identifications are obtained by restricting the same ring sheaf $\Lambda_T$ to the slice at $V$; iterated restriction of that sheaf is literal restriction along the composite. Equivalently, the two fibre-product maps have equal projections to $V$ and $S$, as in step 3. Thus the two module maps agree in every degree and after localization. For an identity open the same calculation is already the identity. For an identity scheme morphism its direct-image comparison acts on $I^n(V)$ as the identity, so the unit constraints in clause 1 also hold.

source.place: Canonicity and associativity: restrictions of comparisons are identities, including identity constraints

proof.text: For clause 3 fix $I$ on $X$. The complexes $f_*I$, $(gf)_*I$, $j_X^*I$, and $(f_U)_*j_X^*I$ are K-injective by step 1. Hence every factor in the displayed equation is computed without another replacement, using steps 2 and 5. At $V\to U$ in degree $n$, its left-hand path first replaces $(gf)_*I$ by $g_*f_*I$, then restricts $g$ to $U$, then restricts $f$ to $Y_U$. Its right-hand path first restricts $gf$ to $U$, then splits it into $g_U$ and $f_U$. By steps 3 and 4 each path sends a section over $V\times_T X$ to that same section over $(V\times_UY_U)\times_{Y_U}X_U$, via the canonical isomorphism to $V\times_T X$. The two isomorphisms have the same projections to $V$ and $X$, so they are equal by the fibre-product universal property. Thus the paths give equal module chain maps and equal derived maps. Naturality and independence of $I$ follow from step 2 and step 5. This is the precise composition equation in clause 3, with its stated associators and fibre-product identifications.

tool_uses.why: General homological-algebra tool: an exact left adjoint makes its right adjoint preserve K-injectives, needed for a common resolution; no affine-space unit result supplies it.

The resolution-normalized comparison named in the item; used as a general ringed-topos direct-image tool.
General representative and transition formulas for total derived functors; needed to descend the explicit sectionwise maps naturally.
General coefficient-composition identity ensuring that the underived comparisons have the required module actions.
General open-slice base-change isomorphism for arbitrary sheaves of rings; used for the underived comparison, without replacing the unit route.
